title: Infinite trees: branches, König's lemma, and Aronszajn trees

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 68–69 (§16, Lemma 16.1 and Theorem 16.3; finite repair and fresh reserves supplied explicitly)

summary: Finite levels force an infinite path; countable levels at uncountable height can prevent a cofinal path.
abstract: Finite decreasing sequences of natural numbers can be arbitrarily long, although no infinite decreasing sequence exists. König's lemma gives a contrasting result: a tree with levels numbered by the natural numbers, each nonempty and finite, has a path through all of them. The analogous statement fails at the first uncountable height, even when every level is countable. Such a counterexample is called an Aronszajn tree; in the construction here, every individual node still extends to every higher level.
